subject: Voyager Labs - conversation pacing regression causing elongated streaming windows
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex@voyager.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime: noticeable elongation in streaming responses starting ~08:50 PT

Hi Priya / Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in end-to-end response times for our user-facing Live Assist flow at ~08:50 PT today. It looks like streamed tokens are arriving in larger gaps — sessions that normally stream tokens continuously are now taking 2–4s pauses every ~15s, causing the UI to appear frozen. Overall throughput is OK, but the perceived latency is bad for agents.

What we've checked: same client version, no deploy on our side, traffic volume stable. We can share request IDs and a small log bundle if that helps. This is impacting one production region (us-west).

Attaching a small set of request traces (voyager_request_sample.log) to this email. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (config, routing, batching) around that time?

Thanks — we can jump on a call if helpful.

Alex
Ops Lead, Voyager Labs

Attachments: voyager_request_sample.log (text)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex@voyager.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: noticeable elongation in streaming responses starting ~08:50 PT

Hi Alex — thanks for flagging this and for the traces. We're investigating immediately. Quick notes / immediate steps we're taking: 

- I've opened an incident tracker (SRV-1742) and looped in our infra on-call (Jonas).
- Can you please send one full request_id from a slow session and confirm the client-side Accept header (are you using chunked transfer / keep-alive)? That helps narrow whether the pause is client or server side.
- We're going to try a temporary routing tweak: route your traffic to the model-variant with the older kernel/serialization path (no quantized re-batch) to see if it removes the stutter. This is non-disruptive and should be reversible in minutes.

Temporary expectations: we'll test the routing change in the next 10–15 minutes and report back. If you see improvement after we flip it, we may keep it while we root-cause. We will also accept the logs bundle you mentioned.

Thanks — apologies for the disruption. I'll update you within 30 minutes.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Park <alex@voyager.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: noticeable elongation in streaming responses starting ~08:50 PT

Priya / Marissa / Alex — quick tech update. I looked at the edge telemetry and model-host traces for the timeframe. Findings so far: 

- Around 08:48–08:52 PT we have a small spike in continuous-batching rebalancer activity on the us-west serving pool (a kernel selection heuristic default was evaluated and a micro-rollback didn't finish fast enough). That caused a short-lived mixing of two batching paths which can increase time between flushes for long-hold sessions (exactly what you're seeing).
- The easiest immediate mitigation is to pin Voyager's routing to the legacy serialization path (model-variant v3-stable) — this avoids the re-batch heuristic and keeps steady small flush sizes. We can do a safe per-customer route at the edge; no model change required.
- Workaround for client side: reduce the token buffer window to 200ms (from 800ms) if you can change the SDK config; that reduces perceived pauses while we stabilize the runtime.

Action I'll run now (10:00 PT): per-customer routing -> v3-stable for Voyager (canary to 5% then 100% if clean). I'll watch token inter-arrival times and report.

Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Park <alex@voyager.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: noticeable elongation in streaming responses starting ~08:50 PT

Thanks — we saw a big improvement shortly after 09:58 when you reported the canary. The freezing pauses are much reduced; agent UX is back to acceptable levels. We'll send the requested full request_id and the zipped log bundle (voyager_request_logs_20261101.zip) for your postmortem.

A couple of asks from our side: 
- Can you confirm whether this will be kept on v3-stable for us while a root-cause fix is implemented? We want to avoid any black swan roll that might reintroduce the stutter during our peak hours.
- We will need a short post-incident summary for our internal ops team and a note about any potential credit for the window of degraded experience (this is customer-visible).

Appreciate the fast response.

Alex

Attachments: voyager_request_logs_20261101.zip (application/zip)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex@voyager.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: noticeable elongation in streaming responses starting ~08:50 PT

Hi Alex — following up with an interim post-incident note and next steps. Thank you for the logs — they were helpful. Summary and actions: 

- Incident summary (what happened): A batching/kernel selection heuristic evaluation coincided with short-lived rebalancer churn in the us-west serving pool. That mixing led to intermittent larger flush windows for long-lived streaming sessions and produced the 2–4s pauses you observed.
- Impact window: 2026-11-01 08:48–09:02 PT (approx).
- Mitigation taken: We pinned Voyager traffic to model-variant v3-stable at 09:58 PT (canary -> 100% by 10:03 PT). That eliminated the re-batching mixing and restored steady token emission behavior.
- Short-term recommendation for Voyager: keep the client token-buffer window at 200–300ms, and enable retry/backoff for single-chunk timeouts to avoid needless reconnections during residual jitter.
- Next steps on our side:
  - Engineering will roll a non-disruptive fix to the kernel selection heuristic to prevent mixed-path flush behavior (JIRA SRV-1742, target deploy: 2026-11-07).
  - We'll run a coordinated canary with you before the change is promoted to all customers.
  - We'll prepare a formal postmortem and a compensation proposal for the affected window by EOD tomorrow.

I've attached an incident snapshot (redwood_incident_snapshot_20261101.json) with traces/metrics for your records and opened a short 30-minute sync for tomorrow morning if you'd like to review the postmortem draft together.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll follow up with the formal postmortem and the compensation proposal.

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
